\noindent\textbf{How to read this supplement.} The sections follow the main text.
Section, figure and table numbers without the prefix S refer to the main text. Names are
those of the main text: T0 is the history-only estimator, TX the estimator of the paper,
L5 the level of the following frames, F the reading of the frame; D10, D$d$, S and K$k$
are the availability rules; V1 to V4 and M1 to M4 the validation designs. The labels B.73
to B.84 are the registered batches; for each, the registration, the code, the result file
with every readout and the record of the independent recomputation are in the public
repository named in the main text (\texttt{ces\_prediction/experiments/} and
\texttt{docs/paper/}). The supplement of the earlier version of this work, with the
measurement regime of the chord, the rotation of the chord and the design of the
recurrent network, is kept in that repository
(\texttt{docs/paper/ppcf/earlier\_line/}).

\section{The KSTAR files and the reported value}
\label{sec:sdata}

This section gives in full what \S\ref{sec:data} summarizes: the published geometry, how
a row of the files is assembled, the beam files, the rows with a constant ECEI, and the
test on bursts inside the exposure.

  streams of twelve discharges). The CES value of a row is the frame whose exposure starts

\paragraph{The beam files.} For every shot file a second file gives, row by row, the
power, voltage and current of the six sources of the two beam boxes
(Table~\ref{tab:nbisources}). The first source of the first box is never on. An absent
frame is a notch of the two sources of the first box that run
(Table~\ref{tab:nbinotch}); the power in the first row after a notch is a sample taken
while the beam returns. A \Ti{} value is written whichever of those two sources is on. In
the 13 earliest shot files the power columns of the second
box cannot be used (values above 5\,MW or below $-0.1$\,MW); the batch with beam inputs
reads the columns as delivered and shows the refit without those files beside it
(Table~\ref{tab:refit}).

\end{table}

\end{table}

\paragraph{Rows with a constant ECEI.} In part of the discharges the four ECEI channels
have exactly the same values over many rows, while the BES channels move
(Table~\ref{tab:stuck}); the example discharge of the main text is one of them until
about 2\,s. The estimators were fitted and scored with these rows in. Where the ECEI is
constant the fast-channel increment is smaller; leaving the rows out changes the overall
values little, and the last block of shots is not accounted for by them. This is a
description read after the fact, without intervals.

\begin{table}[tbp]
  \centering
  \caption{\CapStuckEcei}
  \label{tab:stuck}
  \TabStuckEcei
\end{table}

\paragraph{Bursts inside the exposure (B.74).} For eleven discharges with raw 500\,kHz
BES, the rows were divided by whether the exposure of the frame (from 2\,ms before the
stamp to 8\,ms after it) contains a burst of BES light, detected by a rule fixed in an
earlier batch. Table~\ref{tab:bursts} gives the registered readouts. A reading that rises
for one frame occurs several times more often in a frame with a burst than the share of
such frames; in those frames the level of the following frames and the rotation from the
same fit do not move, and the reading is more often absent. This says in which frames the
reported width jumps, not whether the ions are hotter in them; spectra, fit amplitudes and
fit errors, which would decide that, are not in the files. The light that varies with the
value lies in the 4\,ms before the stamp, so the fast sample of a row is taken after most
of that light has come in: no estimator here is ahead of the measurement. The bursts are
defined on BES alone (no D-alpha is in the files), and the intervals resample eleven
discharges.

\section{Definitions}
\label{sec:sdefs}

\paragraph{Rows.} Table~\ref{tab:sets} gives the row sets. A segment ends at a gap of 0.5\,s or more; no estimator
reads across it.

\begin{table}[tbp]
  \centering
  \caption{\CapSets}
  \label{tab:sets}
  \TabSets
\end{table}

\paragraph{Rules.} Under D$d$ a value is visible at row $t$ when its stamp is at most
$t - d$, with a tolerance of 3\,ms for the rounding of the stamps (0.5\,ms on MAST).
Under S the visible values are those stamped at or before the last row before the most
recent absent step that ends at or before row $t$; a row with no absent step earlier in
its segment has no visible value under S and is not scored under it. Under K$k$ the frame
index counts 10\,ms frames from the start of the segment, absent frames included, and a
value is visible when its index is a multiple of $k$ and its row is before $t$; the scored
rows are those whose index is a multiple of none of the spacings compared.

\paragraph{Estimators.} The causal GP is evaluated at row $t$ on the last 16 visible
values with a Mat\'ern-3/2 kernel and white noise; the values are standardized within the
neighbour set, and the length scale (5, 10, 20, 40 or 80\,ms) and the noise variance are
chosen at every row by exact marginal likelihood on a fixed grid. The offline GP is the
same process with the 16 nearest values on each side of row $t$, the row itself left out;
PCHIP runs through all measured values of the block with the row left out. The boosted regression
(\texttt{HistGradientBoostingRegressor} of scikit-learn, default settings, fixed seed) is
fitted to the difference between the target and the GP estimate on the fit rows; the
estimate is the GP estimate plus the regression. The ten history scalars are the time
step, the age of the newest visible value, the held value H, the GP estimate minus H and
its absolute value, and of the last up to ten visible values the mean, the standard
deviation, H minus the mean, the last increment and their number. The eight fast scalars
are, for the BES array mean and the ECEI array mean each, the level (the standardized
array mean at row $t$), its departure from the mean of the ten rows before, the standard
deviation over
those rows and the one-row increment. The six anchor scalars are, for each array mean, the
level at the anchor row, the change of the level since the anchor row and the logarithm of
the ratio of the raw running means at row $t$ and at the anchor row. Missing inputs are
passed to the regression as missing. The exact operations are in the registrations of
B.73 and B.75.

\paragraph{Intervals.} For a ratio of mean squared errors the sums of squared errors per
cluster are resampled: 20{,}000 draws of shot clusters with replacement (MAST: sessions);
under V1 and V2 one of the three re-partitions or assignments is drawn first. The
discharge form resamples discharges. Verdicts use the cluster form.

\section{MAST}
\label{sec:smast}

The MAST rows come from the public FAIR-MAST archive~\citep{Jackson2024FairMast}:
charge-exchange \Ti{} in 5\,ms frames and Thomson-scattering profiles of \Te{} and
density. A chord enters at a frame when it lies 1.5 to 5\,cm inside the edge of the
Thomson density profile of that frame; a row needs a good \Ti{} value, a Thomson value at
the chord's radius at frame $t$ and at the anchor frame, and a defined level of the next
five frames. No frame is hidden by a beam modulation, so a delay D$d$ is imposed by
withholding the values younger than $d$. Table~\ref{tab:mast} gives the errors by delay
and Table~\ref{tab:mastcost} the cost of staleness, the increment and the recovered share
by design. A readout with D-alpha as a
further input is in the result file of B.76; its scale is set over the whole shot and is
therefore not causal within a shot, and it is not used here.

\begin{table}[tbp]
  \centering
  \caption{MAST, pedestal-top band, target L5: RMSE by delay of the charge-exchange history under the random (M1) and the chronological design (M4), on the rows complete under all delays. TX adds the Thomson scalars of the same radius. RT multiplies the held value by the ratio of the Thomson $T_e$ at the present and at the anchor frame; RTa fits an exponent $\alpha$ and an offset to that ratio in logarithms.}
  \label{tab:mast}

\section{The nowcast condition: further tables}
\label{sec:sprev}

With the previous frame visible (the nowcast condition, D10), Table~\ref{tab:ladderdesigns}
repeats the estimators of Table~\ref{tab:ladder} on the value of the frame for the other
designs; the two references that wait for the next value, PCHIP and the offline GP, are
computed with the row left out and cannot be formed on the last measured row of a block.
Table~\ref{tab:dten} gives the reductions by the fast inputs by design and target and
Table~\ref{tab:network} every estimator under the random design, among them the recurrent
network and its two-stage form.

\begin{table}[tbp]
  \centering
  \caption{\CapLadderDesigns}
  \label{tab:ladderdesigns}
  \TabLadderDesigns
\end{table}

The recurrent network has two LSTM branches that run forward in time over every grid
row. The \Ti{} branch reads the fast channels, the time step and, per target, the last
observed value, its staleness and an observed flag; it was trained on the reading of the
frame with a masked squared-error loss. The two-stage estimator adds a boosted regression
of the network's error, fitted on out-of-fold errors. With the previous frame visible
these have the same error on the reading of the frame as the network-free estimator, and
a higher error on the level; fitted to the level, the network-free estimator has the
lowest error of the table. On the level, the increment of the fast inputs under D10 is
small and is not established under the rolling-origin design.

\begin{table}[tbp]

\section{Independent recomputation}
\label{sec:schecks}

For every batch a part of the registered readout was recomputed with code written
independently of the implementation; the scripts and their outputs are in the repository
(\texttt{lead\_checks} in the folder of each batch, and the files
\texttt{b7x\_lead\_checks.md}).

Skills in this section are signed fractions, as in the statement tables.

\paragraph{B.75 (stale history).} The statement values were pooled again from the stored
estimates and equal the registered readout. Under D650 the visible values, their age, the
history scalars, the causal GP and the anchor row of all D1 rows were recomputed and equal
the implementation's bit for bit; the fast scalars equal them up to rounding. A fit of TX
on the chronological unit with the recomputed fast scalars gives an increment of $+0.217$
where the stored fit gives $+0.237$: a single-unit value of the last block is sensitive
to the fit at that level, which the registered interval contains.

\paragraph{B.76 (MAST).} The statement values were pooled again and are equal. For 24
shots drawn at random the reported value, the level, the visible history under D100, the
GP and the Thomson values at frame $t$ and at the anchor frame were recomputed from the
shot files and equal the row table exactly; own fits of T0 and TX on the chronological
design reproduce the stored estimates. Not registered, on that design and without
intervals: with the Thomson scalars permuted the skill over T0 is $-0.008$; with the four
\Te{} scalars alone it is $+0.433$ of the $+0.443$, with the four density scalars alone
$+0.170$, and with the distance to the density edge alone $-0.013$.

\paragraph{B.77 and B.78 (correcting the reading; sparse CES).} The statement values were
pooled again and are equal. The frame index, the scored rows and every history input under
K10 were recomputed and equal the cached ones bit for bit, and so do the history-only
fits. With the recomputed fast scalars the increment of the chronological unit under K10
is $+0.033$ where the stored fit gives $+0.023$.

\paragraph{B.79 and B.80 (beam inputs; ECEI coherence).} The 19 beam scalars were rebuilt
from the beam files and equal the cached ones exactly; the statement values of the
registered readout and of the refit without the 13 files were pooled again and are equal.
For B.80 the correlation between the ECEI channels of every discharge, the class counts,
the class skills and the gated estimator were recomputed from the grid and the stored
estimates and are equal.

\paragraph{B.81 (the two controls and the two halves).} The seventeen statement values
and the controls of every design and rule were pooled again from the stored estimates and
are equal. Over the test rows the correction that the permuted fit adds to the
history-only estimate is several times smaller than that of TX and is almost uncorrelated
with it, as it should be when the fit cannot see the fast inputs of the row.

\paragraph{B.82 (where the increment arises; robust measures; specificity; seeds).} The
time since the last notch was recomputed from the grid stamps and equals the batch's on
every row; the increments by its classes, the robust measures of the random design, the
pooled values of the specificity controls and the seed spread were recomputed from the
stored estimates and are equal.

\paragraph{B.83 (the nowcast against the interpolation that waits).} PCHIP was recomputed
with an independent implementation on the rows of 60 discharges drawn at random, through
every measured value of the row's block with the row left out, and equals the batch's
reference exactly on all but two of them; those two lie beside a stretch without a kept
row, where the block of the reference ends and the grid segment does not. The statement
values were recomputed from the stored estimates and the references and are equal.

\paragraph{B.84 (is the second stage bound to rules).} The eleven statement values, the
RMSE values of the per-rule, applied, single-fit, raw-window and level-free estimators and
the increment of the single fit along the rules were pooled again from the stored
estimates and are equal.
